items.title: ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Lead 2026 TCA Awards: Full Winners List
items.summary:
The Television Critics Association handed its Program of the Year prize to HBO Max's Heated Rivalry on Thursday, capping the 42nd annual TCA Awards. Apple TV's Widow's Bay took home the most trophies of any single show with three, including Outstanding Comedy, and HBO Max's The Pitt won Outstanding Achievement in Drama.

Widow's Bay, a first-year series, also won Outstanding New Program and Individual Achievement in Comedy for star Kate O'Flynn. Rhea Seehorn won Individual Achievement in Drama for Apple TV's Pluribus. Both actresses head into next month's Emmys as nominees, with Widow's Bay carrying 19 Emmy nominations and The Pitt leading the current field with 25.

Heated Rivalry's win comes with an asterisk of sorts. As Deadline reported, the series is ineligible for Emmy consideration because Canadian company Crave, a Bell Media outfit, fully funded and produced it, and Television Academy rules require a U.S. partner to be intrinsically involved in production.

Elsewhere on the list, Netflix's Death by Lightning won Outstanding Achievement in Movies, Miniseries or Specials, and Peacock's The Traitors took the Reality category. The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, which recently wrapped its CBS run, won Outstanding Achievement in Variety, Talk or Sketch, while PBS's The American Revolution won in News and Information.

Netflix picked up two more wins with Long Story Short in Animation and Squid Game for International Series. Disney+'s Percy Jackson and the Olympians won Family Programming, and Apple TV's Snoopy Presents: A Summer Musical won Children's Programming.

The organization also named its special honorees. Colbert received the 2026 Career Achievement Award, and the sketch comedy series In Living Color, which ran from 1990 to 1994, was recognized for its influence.

items.title: Phoebe Bridgers Covers Nirvana In The Live Lounge
items.summary:
Phoebe Bridgers recorded a session for BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge in London, and the footage is now available. She performed "Lost Boys," a single from her new album Lost Weekend, along with "Bobby," and covered Nirvana's "Lithium."

The session arrives at an awkward moment in her schedule. Bridgers postponed a run of intimate UK shows this week after a bout of appendicitis, which would have been her first live performances since Lost Weekend arrived last Friday. She taped the Live Lounge visit before the appendix flared up.

The "Bobby" performance carries some added weight for fans. As Stereogum noted, Bridgers has banned phones from her shows this year, so the Live Lounge footage is the first publicly circulating performance video of the song, which has become a favorite among listeners.

The Nirvana cover connects to a longer thread in Bridgers' career. Her supergroup boygenius recreated a well-known Nirvana Rolling Stone photo shoot for their own cover story, and Dave Grohl later joined the trio onstage at the Hollywood Bowl to play "Satanist" from The Record.

Bridgers has not announced rescheduled dates for the postponed UK shows. The Live Lounge session stands as the only new live material from her since the album's release.

items.title: Jack White and Charley Crockett Are Beefing
items.summary:
Jack White and Charley Crockett spent this week trading insults on Instagram, the latest turn in a dispute that began when Crockett dropped the Satanic doo-wop duo Twin Temple from his Age of the Ram tour in July. The band said they were cut "due to their Satanic imagery." Crockett offered his own version at the time: "I thought they were like Black Sabbath, but they ain't. Not today, Satan."

White subsequently invited Twin Temple to open his Los Angeles show, which drew national attention to the duo and led to their late-night television debut. The story had quieted down until August 18, when Crockett posted, then deleted, an Instagram message meant to "clear this up right quick."

In that post, Crockett accused Twin Temple of inventing the Satanic imagery explanation and said other musicians who had praised him for years turned on him. He then went after White directly: "[H]e used it to sell tickets too and I lost a lot of respect for him. I wonder why he wasn't so outspoken back when he was in the White Stripes 20 something years ago. They purposely avoided political issues."

White answered with a post consisting largely of the lyrics to "Rappin Duke," the 1984 Shawn Brown novelty rap, prefaced by a note that Crockett was "trying to drag me into this here rodeo again." As Pitchfork reported, Crockett came back with a response calling White "Mr. Suzy Cream Puff" and "big hoss," clarifying that his political criticism referred to White's "public statements back when it was on the line in 2003," and adding, "Lemme guess, you got Che Guevara and Malcolm X on your shelf, maybe even Fred Hampton, but at the end of the day you get in the Lamborghini and put your kids in private school."

All three acts are working through busy touring years. Crockett is out behind his June album Age of the Ram, White is playing sold-out rooms in support of July's Frozen Charlotte through the end of the year, and Twin Temple release Doomed Lovers on October 9 via Pentagrammaton.

items.title: Anderson .Paak and Cordae Reveal Joint Album
items.summary:
Anderson .Paak and Cordae have made a joint album. Heavy Is the Crown arrives October 23 through Apeshit, Mass Appeal and Empire, and the two have released the cover art, which draws on the 2008 Will Ferrell and John C. Reilly comedy Step Brothers.

The pairing has been building for years. Pitchfork noted that the two first worked together on "RNP" from Cordae's 2019 debut The Lost Boy and have collaborated regularly since.

Cordae's most recent solo album, The Crossroads, came out in 2024. Paak has kept a heavier schedule in the same window, releasing a second NxWorries record, opening for his Silk Sonic bandmate Bruno Mars on tour, and turning up on tracks by Fred Again.., Amber Mark, Summer Walker and Disclosure.

No tracklist or singles have been announced. The album is set for release in October.

items.title: Chris Pratt’s James Reece Is On A Road To Redemption In ‘The Terminal List’ Season 2 Trailer
items.summary:
Prime Video released the first trailer for the second season of The Terminal List, which picks up with Chris Pratt's James Reece looking for redemption after the events of the first season. "Before he was a fugitive, James Reece made a career out of putting terrorists in the dirt," a voiceover says in the trailer. "He may be exactly what we need for this fight."

The new season adapts True Believer, the second novel in Jack Carr's bestselling series. Where the first season worked as a psychological revenge thriller, this one moves into espionage territory, following Reece across the Indian Ocean, Southern and Northern Africa, the Middle East and Europe as he traces a conspiracy running from Moscow to Langley that connects to his own family history.

Tom Hopper returns as Raife Hastings, alongside Constance Wu as Katie Buranek, Dar Salim as Mohammed Farooq and Luke Hemsworth as Jules Landry. Gabriel Luna joins the cast as Freddy Strain, and the expanded international ensemble includes Costa Ronin, Olga Kurylenko, Yul Vazquez, Martin Sensmeier, Arnold Vosloo, Jeremy Bobb and Shiraz Tzarfati.

Pratt executive produces through Indivisible Productions with showrunner David DiGilio, Carr, Antoine Fuqua and Kat Samick of Fuqua Films, former Army Ranger and writer Max Adams, and former Navy SEAL Jared Shaw, who also writes, acts and serves as technical advisor. Amazon MGM Studios, MRC and Civic Center Media produce.

According to Deadline, all eight episodes drop at once on Wednesday, October 21, streaming on Prime Video in more than 240 countries and territories.
